# Set Up

## Load Libraries

```{r library}
suppressMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(readr)
  library(lme4)
  library(lmerTest)
  library(broom.mixed)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(tidyr)
  library(knitr)
})

base_dir <- rprojroot::find_root(
  rprojroot::has_dir("AD_CR_HRS"),
  path = here::here()
)
analysis_dir <- file.path(base_dir, "AD_CR_HRS")
data_dir <- file.path(analysis_dir, "data")
save_dir <- file.path(analysis_dir, "analysis-results")
```

# Define Functions

## Predicted Change Plot

```{r func_pred_change}
plot_change_ptau0 <- function(
    fit,
    outcome_label,
    t_end = 6.25,
    show_ci = FALSE,
    ci_level = 0.95
) {

  # Model data
  mf <- stats::model.frame(fit)

  # One baseline row per participant
  ref <- mf[mf$time == 0, , drop = FALSE]

  # Explicit covariate reference values, following the adjusted ADNI plots.
  # Standardized age is fixed at 0; categorical covariates use the most
  # common observed category; education uses the fitted sample mean.
  most_common <- function(x) {
    tab <- table(x, useNA = "no")
    value <- names(tab)[which.max(tab)]

    if (is.factor(x)) {
      factor(value, levels = levels(x))
    } else if (is.numeric(x)) {
      as.numeric(value)
    } else {
      value
    }
  }

  gender_ref <- most_common(ref$Gender)
  apoe4_ref <- most_common(ref$APOE4)
  education_ref <- mean(ref$Education, na.rm = TRUE)

  # Construct one explicit reference profile for the model-based contrasts.
  reference_profile <- ref[1, , drop = FALSE]
  reference_profile$baseline_age_z <- 0
  reference_profile$Gender <- gender_ref
  reference_profile$APOE4 <- apoe4_ref
  reference_profile$Education <- education_ref
  reference_profile$baseline_pTau <- 0

  reference_values_caption <- sprintf(
    paste0(
      "At age z = 0; Gender = %s; APOE4 = %s; ",
      "education = %.2f; baseline pTau181 z = 0."
    ),
    as.character(gender_ref),
    as.character(apoe4_ref),
    education_ref
  )

  # Fixed-effect coefficients
  b <- lme4::fixef(fit)

  # Fixed-effects model formula/design matrix
  tt <- stats::delete.response(
    stats::terms(fit, fixed.only = TRUE)
  )

  contrasts_used <- attr(
    lme4::getME(fit, "X"),
    "contrasts"
  )

  make_X <- function(d) {
    X <- stats::model.matrix(
      tt,
      d,
      contrasts.arg = contrasts_used
    )

    X[, names(b), drop = FALSE]
  }

  # Estimate annual change at MRS = -1, 0, +1
  # while fixing baseline pTau181 z = 0
  slopes <- do.call(
    rbind,
    lapply(c(-1, 0, 1), function(m) {

      # Prediction profile at baseline
      d0 <- reference_profile
      d0$mrs_z <- m
      d0$time <- 0

      # Same profile one year later
      d1 <- d0
      d1$time <- 1

      # Fixed-effect contrast for one year of change
      D <- make_X(d1) - make_X(d0)

      # One explicit reference profile is used for the contrast.
      L <- as.numeric(D[1, ])

      # Estimate annual change and CI
      ans <- lmerTest::contest1D(
        fit,
        L = L,
        ddf = "Satterthwaite",
        confint = TRUE,
        level = ci_level
      )

      data.frame(
        mrs_z = m,
        baseline_pTau = 0,
        annual_change = ans[["Estimate"]],
        SE = ans[["Std. Error"]],
        df = ans[["df"]],
        lower = ans[["lower"]],
        upper = ans[["upper"]]
      )
    })
  )

  # Convert annual slopes into change over follow-up
  times <- seq(0, t_end, length.out = 101)

  pred <- do.call(
    rbind,
    lapply(seq_len(nrow(slopes)), function(i) {

      data.frame(
        time = times,
        mrs_z = slopes$mrs_z[i],
        baseline_pTau = 0,
        change = times * slopes$annual_change[i],
        lower = times * slopes$lower[i],
        upper = times * slopes$upper[i]
      )
    })
  )

  # Labels and appearance
  labels <- c(
    "MRS = +1",
    "MRS = 0",
    "MRS = -1"
  )

  pred$MRS <- factor(
    pred$mrs_z,
    levels = c(1, 0, -1),
    labels = labels
  )

  colours <- setNames(
    c("#0072B2", "#009E73", "#D62728"),
    labels
  )

  types <- setNames(
    c("solid", "dotted", "longdash"),
    labels
  )

  # Plot
  p <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    pred,
    ggplot2::aes(
      x = time,
      y = change,
      colour = MRS,
      group = MRS
    )
  )

  if (show_ci) {
    p <- p +
      ggplot2::geom_ribbon(
        ggplot2::aes(
          ymin = lower,
          ymax = upper,
          fill = MRS
        ),
        colour = NA,
        alpha = 0.10,
        show.legend = FALSE
      )
  }

  p <- p +
    ggplot2::geom_hline(
      yintercept = 0,
      colour = "grey70",
      linewidth = 0.4
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_line(
      ggplot2::aes(linetype = MRS),
      linewidth = 1.1
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(
      data = pred[pred$time == t_end, ],
      size = 2.5,
      show.legend = FALSE
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = colours) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = colours) +
    ggplot2::scale_linetype_manual(values = types) +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title = paste0("Predicted change in ", outcome_label),
      subtitle = "Reduced model; baseline pTau181 z = 0",
      x = "Years since baseline",
      y = "Predicted memory change (score units)",
      colour = "Standardized MRS",
      linetype = "Standardized MRS",
      caption = reference_values_caption
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme_classic(base_size = 13) +
    ggplot2::theme(
      legend.position = "top",
      plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold"),
      plot.caption = ggplot2::element_text(
        hjust = 0,
        size = 9,
        margin = ggplot2::margin(t = 8)
      )
    )

  list(
    plot = p,
    predictions = pred,
    annual_slopes = slopes,
    reference_values = data.frame(
      baseline_age_z = 0,
      Gender = as.character(gender_ref),
      APOE4 = as.character(apoe4_ref),
      Education = education_ref,
      baseline_pTau = 0
    )
  )
}
```

## Participant Selection

```{r func_subjects}
# Participants with a nonmissing `outcome` score at both visits
get_complete_subjects <- function(stat_df, outcome) {
  stat_df %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data[[outcome]])) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(.data$HHIDPN) %>%
    dplyr::filter(dplyr::n() == 2) %>%
    dplyr::pull("HHIDPN") %>%
    unique()
}
```

## Spaghetti Plot

```{r func_spaghetti}
# Participant trajectories of `outcome`, colored by MRS tertile, with a linear
# trend per tertile. zero_line = TRUE adds a dashed line at 0.
plot_mrs_spaghetti <- function(
    plot_data, outcome, title, y_label, zero_line = FALSE
) {
  p <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    plot_data,
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(
      x = time,
      y = .data[[outcome]],
      group = HHIDPN,
      color = MRS.group
    )
  )

  if (zero_line) {
    p <- p + ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed")
  }

  p +
    ggplot2::geom_line(alpha = 0.35, linewidth = 1.1) +     # thicker spaghetti lines
    ggplot2::geom_point(alpha = 0.25, size = 1.0) +         # slightly larger points
    ggplot2::geom_smooth(
      mapping = ggplot2::aes(
        group = MRS.group,
        color = MRS.group
      ),
      method = "lm",
      formula = y ~ x,
      se = FALSE,
      linewidth = 1.8
    ) +  # thicker trends
    ggplot2::labs(
      title = title,
      x = "Time since baseline (years)",
      y = y_label,
      color = "MRS category"
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
}
```

## Baseline Tables

```{r func_tables}
# Short MRS tertile labels ("Low MRS" -> "Low"), followed by `suffix`
short_mrs_group <- function(mrs_group, suffix = "") {
  dplyr::recode(
    as.character(mrs_group),
    "Low MRS" = paste0("Low", suffix),
    "Mid MRS" = paste0("Mid", suffix),
    "High MRS" = paste0("High", suffix)
  )
}
```

# Load Data

```{r load}
pheno_df <- read.csv(file.path(save_dir, "mrs", "pheno_data.csv"))

pheno_df <- pheno_df %>%
  dplyr::mutate(HHIDPN = paste0(.data$HHID, "_", .data$PN)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data$time))

time_df <- rbind(
  pheno_df %>%
    dplyr::select("HHIDPN", SUT_MEM = "SUT_MEM_16", OSHEA_MEM = "OSHEA_MEM_16") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(time = 0),
  pheno_df %>%
    dplyr::select("HHIDPN", SUT_MEM = "SUT_MEM_22", OSHEA_MEM = "OSHEA_MEM_22", "time")
)

pheno_df <- pheno_df %>%
  dplyr::select(
    "HHIDPN",
    "Gender",
    baseline_age = "Age",
    "Education",
    "APOE4",
    "mrs",
    baseline_pTau = "Z_PTAU181"
  )

stat_df <- pheno_df %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    time_df,
    by = "HHIDPN",
    relationship = "one-to-many",
    na_matches = "never"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    HHIDPN = factor(.data$HHIDPN),
    Gender = factor(.data$Gender),
    mrs_z = as.numeric(scale(.data$mrs)),
    baseline_age_z = as.numeric(scale(.data$baseline_age))
  )
```

# Add MRS Tertiles

```{r tertile}
mrs_cutoffs <- stats::quantile(stat_df$mrs_z, probs = c(1/3, 2/3), na.rm = TRUE)

stat_df <- stat_df %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    MRS.group = cut(
      mrs_z,
      breaks = c(-Inf, mrs_cutoffs[1], mrs_cutoffs[2], Inf),
      labels = c("Low MRS", "Mid MRS", "High MRS"),
      include.lowest = TRUE, right = TRUE
    ),
    MRS.group = factor(MRS.group, levels = c("High MRS", "Mid MRS", "Low MRS"))
  )

stat_df %>%
  dplyr::distinct(.data$HHIDPN, .data$MRS.group) %>%
  dplyr::count(.data$MRS.group)
```

## Get Targets to use per memory

```{r targets}
sut_ls <- get_complete_subjects(stat_df, "SUT_MEM")
oshea_ls <- get_complete_subjects(stat_df, "OSHEA_MEM")
```

# Mixed-Effect Models

## Reduced Model

### Sutin

```{r reduced_sutin}
sf <- lmerTest::lmer(
  SUT_MEM ~ baseline_age_z + Gender + APOE4 + Education + mrs_z + baseline_pTau +
    mrs_z*time + baseline_pTau*time + mrs_z*baseline_pTau +
    (1 | HHIDPN),
  data = stat_df %>% dplyr::filter(.data$HHIDPN %in% sut_ls),
  REML = TRUE
)
summary(sf)
```

### Oshea

```{r reduced_oshea}
of <- lmerTest::lmer(
  OSHEA_MEM ~ baseline_age_z + Gender + APOE4 + Education + mrs_z + baseline_pTau +
    mrs_z*time + baseline_pTau*time + mrs_z*baseline_pTau +
    (1 | HHIDPN),
  data = stat_df %>% dplyr::filter(.data$HHIDPN %in% oshea_ls),
  REML = TRUE
)
summary(of)
```

## Full Model

### Sutin

```{r full_sutin}
sg <- lmerTest::lmer(
  SUT_MEM ~ baseline_age_z + Gender + APOE4 + Education + mrs_z*time*baseline_pTau +
    (1 | HHIDPN),
  data = stat_df %>% dplyr::filter(.data$HHIDPN %in% sut_ls),
  REML = TRUE
)
summary(sg)
```

### Oshea

```{r full_oshea}
og <- lmerTest::lmer(
  OSHEA_MEM ~ baseline_age_z + Gender + APOE4 + Education + mrs_z*time*baseline_pTau +
    (1 | HHIDPN),
  data = stat_df %>% dplyr::filter(.data$HHIDPN %in% oshea_ls),
  REML = TRUE
)
summary(og)
```

## By MRS Tertiles

### Sutin

```{r tertile_sutin}
sf_cat <- lmerTest::lmer(
  SUT_MEM ~ baseline_age_z + Gender + APOE4 + Education + MRS.group + baseline_pTau +
    MRS.group*time + baseline_pTau*time + MRS.group*baseline_pTau +
    (1 | HHIDPN),
  data = stat_df %>% dplyr::filter(.data$HHIDPN %in% sut_ls),
  REML = TRUE
)
summary(sf_cat)
```

### OSHEA

```{r tertile_oshea}
of_cat <- lmerTest::lmer(
  OSHEA_MEM ~ baseline_age_z + Gender + APOE4 + Education + MRS.group + baseline_pTau +
    MRS.group*time + baseline_pTau*time + MRS.group*baseline_pTau +
    (1 | HHIDPN),
  data = stat_df %>% dplyr::filter(.data$HHIDPN %in% oshea_ls),
  REML = TRUE
)
summary(of_cat)
```

## Change-from-Baseline Plot (ΔMEM)

### Calculate Baselines

```{r baselines}
baseline_df <- stat_df %>%
  dplyr::filter(.data$time == 0) %>%
  dplyr::select("HHIDPN", SUT_baseline = "SUT_MEM", OSHEA_baseline = "OSHEA_MEM")

plot_df <- stat_df %>%
  dplyr::left_join(baseline_df, by = "HHIDPN") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    SUT_change = .data$SUT_MEM - .data$SUT_baseline,
    OSHEA_change = .data$OSHEA_MEM - .data$OSHEA_baseline
  )
```

### Sutin

```{r spaghetti_change_sutin}
plot_mrs_spaghetti(
  plot_df %>% dplyr::filter(.data$HHIDPN %in% sut_ls),
  outcome = "SUT_change",
  title = "Change in Sutin Memory from baseline by MRS tertile",
  y_label = "Δ Sutin Memory from baseline",
  zero_line = TRUE
)
```

### O'Shea

# Baseline Comparisons by MRS

## Continuous Variables

```{r baseline_cont}
cont_vars <- c("baseline_age", "Education", "baseline_pTau", "time")

cont_long <- stat_df %>%
  dplyr::filter(.data$time != 0) %>%
  dplyr::select("MRS.group", dplyr::all_of(cont_vars)) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = dplyr::all_of(cont_vars),
    names_to = "Variable",
    values_to = "value"
  )

# Kruskal–Wallis p per variable
kw_df <- cont_long %>%
  dplyr::group_by(.data$Variable) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    `Kruskal-Wallis p` = tryCatch(
      stats::kruskal.test(value ~ MRS.group)$p.value, error = function(e) NA_real_
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Total N (non-missing across all groups) per variable
totals_cont <- cont_long %>%
  dplyr::group_by(.data$Variable) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    `Total N` = sum(!is.na(.data$value)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Group summaries and pretty string (use actual ±, not \u escapes)
cont_summ <- cont_long %>%
  dplyr::group_by(.data$Variable, .data$MRS.group) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    N      = sum(!is.na(.data$value)),
    Mean   = mean(.data$value, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD     = stats::sd(.data$value,   na.rm = TRUE),
    Median = stats::median(.data$value, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    grp = short_mrs_group(.data$MRS.group),
    pretty = sprintf("%.2f ± %.2f (%.2f)", Mean, SD, Median)
  )

# Wide: one row per variable; columns like "Low N", "Low pretty", etc.
cont_table_wide <- cont_summ %>%
  dplyr::select("Variable", "grp", "N", "pretty") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = "grp",
    values_from = c("N", "pretty"),
    names_glue = "{grp} {.value}"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    totals_cont,
    by = "Variable",
    relationship = "one-to-one",
    na_matches = "never"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    kw_df,
    by = "Variable",
    relationship = "one-to-one",
    na_matches = "never"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::relocate(.data[["Total N"]], .after = .data$Variable)

# Show
knitr::kable(
  cont_table_wide,
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Continuous variables by MRS tertile (wide): N and mean±SD (median), with Total N and Kruskal–Wallis p."
)
```

## Categorical Variables

```{r baseline_cat}
## =========================
## Categorical (wide, pretty)
## =========================
cat_long <- stat_df %>%
  dplyr::filter(.data$time != 0) %>%
  dplyr::select("MRS.group", "Gender", "APOE4") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(APOE4 = factor(.data$APOE4, levels = c(0, 1, 2))) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c("Gender", "APOE4"),
    names_to = "Variable",
    values_to = "Level"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Level = factor(.data$Level))

# Counts/percents within each MRS group
cat_counts <- cat_long %>%
  dplyr::count(.data$Variable, .data$Level, .data$MRS.group, name = "Count") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(.data$Variable, .data$MRS.group) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Percent = 100 * .data$Count / sum(.data$Count)) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

# Fisher’s exact p across Low/Mid/High (one p per variable)
fisher_df <- cat_long %>%
  dplyr::group_by(.data$Variable) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    `Fisher p` = tryCatch(
      stats::fisher.test(table(.data$MRS.group, .data$Level))$p.value, error = function(e) NA_real_
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Total N across groups per Variable–Level
totals_cat <- cat_counts %>%
  dplyr::group_by(.data$Variable, .data$Level) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(`Total N` = sum(.data$Count), .groups = "drop")

# Pretty wide table with n(%) and Total N
cat_table_wide <- cat_counts %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    grp = short_mrs_group(.data$MRS.group),
    `n(%)` = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", .data$Count, .data$Percent)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select("Variable", "Level", "grp", "n(%)") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = "grp", values_from = "n(%)") %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    totals_cat,
    by = c("Variable", "Level"),
    relationship = "one-to-one",
    na_matches = "never"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    fisher_df,
    by = "Variable",
    relationship = "many-to-one",
    na_matches = "never"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::relocate(.data[["Total N"]], .after = "Level")

# Add group denominators (Ns) to the categorical wide table
group_Ns <- cat_long %>%
  dplyr::group_by(.data$Variable, .data$MRS.group) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(Group_N = sum(!is.na(.data$Level)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(col = short_mrs_group(.data$MRS.group, suffix = "_N")) %>%
  dplyr::select(-"MRS.group") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = "col", values_from = "Group_N")

cat_table_wide <- cat_table_wide %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    group_Ns,
    by = "Variable",
    relationship = "many-to-one",
    na_matches = "never"
  )

# Show
knitr::kable(
  cat_table_wide,
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Categorical variables by MRS tertile (wide): n(%) with Total N and Fisher’s exact p."
)
```
